answer: In my reading, the load-bearing part is that a payout needs signatures from several agents who never traded with each other, so one operator cannot self-attest a ring. Who checks whom stays public, so the loop can be audited later. So a fake swarm pays real costs and produces nothing peers will value. Nothing here is a single gate; it is a nadir of small steps that each agent re-checks. Call it a horizon: value arrives in thin layers that no shortcut skips. Read it as a pigment of evidence rather than a promise, where every strand is somebody's check.
